In SQL Server, SUM(Amount) {{c1::OVER}} (PARTITION BY CustomerID) calculates a total alongside each customer's rows.
column2:
OVER makes this an aggregate window expression.
Review source

column1: To total Amount separately per customer, use SUM(Amount) OVER ({{c1::PARTITION BY CustomerID}}).
column2:
Each customer's rows form a separate partition.
Review source

column1: With unique ProductID, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ({{c1::ORDER BY Price DESC, ProductID}}) numbers highest prices first and breaks ties by ProductID.
column2:
The unique key makes assignments among equal prices repeatable for unchanged data.
Review source

column1: For SQL Server SUM with window ORDER BY but no explicit frame, the default is {{c1::RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW}}.
column2:
RANGE includes all rows tied with the current row on the window ordering values.
Review source

column1: To divide products into four roughly equal-sized price groups, use {{c1::NTILE(4)}} OVER (ORDER BY Price DESC).
column2:
Group 1 contains the first rows in the descending price order.
Review source

column1: With unique OrderID, a row-by-row running total uses SUM(Amount) OVER (ORDER BY OrderID {{c1::ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW}}).
column2:
The frame includes all preceding rows and the current row.
Review source

column1: With unique OrderID, AVG(Amount) OVER (ORDER BY OrderID ROWS BETWEEN {{c1::2 PRECEDING}} AND CURRENT ROW) averages up to three orders.
column2:
At the partition start, the frame contains only the available rows.
Review source

column1: A frame covering the current row and up to two following rows uses ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND {{c1::2 FOLLOWING}}.
column2:
Following rows are determined by the window ORDER BY.
Review source

column1: When omitted, the row offset for LAG and LEAD defaults to {{c1::1}}.
column2:
The functions look one row backward or forward within the partition.
Review source

column1: On a partition's first row, LAG(Amount) OVER (ORDER BY OrderID) returns {{c1::NULL}}.
column2:
No preceding row exists, and the call supplies no alternative default.
Review source

column1: With unique OrderID, change from the previous amount uses Amount - {{c1::LAG(Amount,1,0)}} OVER (ORDER BY OrderID).
column2:
The first row compares against the supplied default of 0.
Review source

column1: To read Amount two rows ahead, use LEAD(Amount,{{c1::2}},0) OVER (ORDER BY OrderID).
column2:
The supplied 0 applies when the requested following row is outside the partition.
Review source

column1: With unique OrderID and default NULL handling, {{c1::FIRST_VALUE(Amount)}} OVER (ORDER BY OrderID) returns the first ordered Amount.
column2:
The default frame starts at the beginning of the partition.
Review source

column1: With unique OrderID, LAST_VALUE(Amount) OVER (ORDER BY OrderID {{c1::ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING}}) reaches the partition's final row.
column2:
The explicit frame includes the entire partition.
Review source

column1: The first row of any SQL Server PERCENT_RANK partition has a result of {{c1::0}}.
column2:
Rows tied with the first ordering value also share the lowest relative rank.
Review source

column1: For one partition containing ascending values 10,20,20, CUME_DIST() gives both 20 rows {{c1::1.0}}.
column2:
All three values are at or below 20, so the fraction is 3/3.
Review source

column1: SQL Server ranking functions reject {{c1::ROWS and RANGE}} frame clauses.
column2:
Ranking uses the partition and its ordering rather than an aggregate-style frame.
Review source

column1: In LAG(Amount,1,0), the final argument supplies {{c1::the value for a missing preceding row}}.
column2:
It does not replace NULL in an existing preceding row.
Review source
